DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

They Cried in 1955

STS-HS11-L3-1400P-HSVPAMA1112-TTM-LAT-01 • HS Media Arts 11–12 • Intent, Meaning, and Reception of Media Artworks
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Your mission: travel back to March 1955, to a movie palace on Broadway in Los Angeles. In those years, theaters there showed films from Mexico's Golden Age of cinema to packed crowds of Mexican American families, and many people in the seats lived far from the towns where they grew up. A song about a faraway home could bring a whole row to tears. When Paloma's class watched the same scene this week, most of them laughed.
Why would the same scene make one audience cry and another audience laugh?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Paloma doing?
Look at the picture. Using precise language, what is Paloma's action, and how does it help the team study how an audience responded?
2
What is Emiliano holding?
Look at the picture. Using precise language, what does Emiliano hold, and why is it valuable as a record of that opening night?
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Using precise language, what is the teacher's action, and what does it make possible for the class?
4
What place is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Using precise language, what kind of place is this, and what role did places like it play for audiences in 1955?
5
Tell me about the audience board.
Look at the picture. Using precise language, what does the board document, and what shift in reception does it reveal?
6
What is Renata wearing?
Look at the picture. Using precise language, what is Renata wearing, and how does her clothing serve the time travel mission?
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
